title: Toffee Crunch Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Brown sugar custard with chopped hard butter toffee folded through; cold-start method with the yolks and sugar whisked in the pan.
summary: Based on our classic French custard, this version uses part brown sugar for a deeper caramel taste and has chopped butter toffee folded through after churning. Each spoonful has a little crunch.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
hard butter toffee, chopped into small pieces

steps.title: Make a paste
steps.text: In the saucepan, whisk the yolks with the brown and caster sugars and 2 tbsp of the milk until smooth, with no lumps of sugar.

steps.title: Add the liquid
steps.text: Gradually whisk in the remaining milk and then the cream.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir over medium-low heat until the custard reaches 77-80 °C. Draw a finger across the coated spatula: a clean line means it is ready.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in the salt and vanilla.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Strain, cool in the iced water and refrigerate for at least 4 h, or overnight for the best texture.

steps.title: Prepare the toffee
steps.text: Chop the toffee into mostly pea-sized pieces with a few larger shards, and keep them in the freezer until needed.

steps.title: Churn and fold
steps.text: Churn the custard, fold in the frozen toffee quickly, then freeze for at least 4 h.

tips: Check the toffee label: choose a gelatine-free hard butter toffee, not a soft chewy caramel.
A common mistake is folding in room-temperature toffee, which sticks together. Freeze it first.
For the cleanest pieces, put the toffee in a freezer bag and tap it with a rolling pin.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 2 weeks. The toffee slowly softens after about a week.
